pages.text: The falling river made a wide sandy shore, with nothing to trip over. Raju flew a kite.
Beside Raju, Mina opened and closed empty hands. Raju held the string. Mina wished for a kite of their own.
Mom put on shoes to visit the market. "Do you need anything?" Raju answered quickly, "Thread!"
Mina raised a hand, too, then quietly lowered it. Their mouth stayed firmly shut.
That evening, Mom returned. Thread came out of her bundle, and sweets, too.
Nothing for Mina. Sitting on the sand, Mina only watched Raju's kite.
Mom sat beside Mina. "Why did you lower the hand you raised earlier?"
Mina said, "I'd like a kite, too." Their voice shook a little.
On the next market day, Mina's kite arrived. The wind lifted it high—higher than Raju's.
